newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh deploys army to guard power stations.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh deploys army to guard power stations.

text.p: Bangladesh has deployed troops to guard key electric power plants amid suspicion of sabotage by anti-government forces, the Bengali daily Bhorer Kagoj reported on Wednesday.

The newspaper, quoting Energy Minister Nooruddin Khan, said the army was handling security at the three key power generation plants in southern district of Khulna and in the eastern areas of Ghorasal and Ashuganj.
Energy Ministry officials said a 50-member army contingent was guarding the Goalpara Power Station in Khulna.
They said the unprecedented security move followed detection of mysterious damage to power grid towers at different points in recent weeks.
Two towers of the national power grid collapsed in the northern district of Pabna on March 15 and an official investigation said it was an act of sabotage.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has openly charged the main opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) with subversive activities.
Acute power shortages in recent months have triggered widespread public discontent, but Khan said he hoped the situation would improve soon.
"The situation has already started improving with power plants shut down for disruption in supply of natural gas resuming operation," one ministry official said on Wednesday.
He said the daily power output was currently 1,700 megawatts against demand of 2,000 megawatts, leaving a shortfall of 300 megawatts.

Bhorer Kagoj quoted Energy Minister Khan as saying that power generation would markedly improve next month when a newly constructed gas pipeline would fuel a 210 megawatt power plant in the port city of Chittagong.
